entries.title: UNIT 10 WOODHURST | Chatsworth From Above
entries.description:
🚁 CHATSWORTH FROM ABOVE | EPISODE 10 — WOODHURST

Our journey through Chatsworth continues, and we've now arrived at UNIT 10 — WOODHURST!

Following our previous episode exploring Moorton and Risecliff, we're taking to the skies over another fascinating part of Chatsworth, Durban.

From one of the area's most recognisable hospitals to its public park, schools, municipal flats and industrial businesses, Woodhurst has a unique story to tell.

But how did Woodhurst get its name? And what makes Unit 10 different from the other neighbourhoods we've explored?

Join me as we uncover the history, landmarks and community life of Woodhurst through breathtaking aerial footage and local storytelling.

📍 PLACES AND LANDMARKS FEATURED

🏥 CHATSMED GARDEN HOSPITAL

One of Woodhurst's most recognisable landmarks, Life Chatsmed Garden Hospital has served Chatsworth and surrounding communities for decades. Located along Woodhurst Drive, the hospital is an important part of the area's healthcare history.

🌳 UNIT 10 PARK — WOODHURST PARK

A familiar recreational space that holds memories for generations of Woodhurst residents. We take a look at the park from above and explore its role within the community.

🏭 SUNSET AVENUE — INDUSTRIAL AREA

Discover another side of Woodhurst, where factories, workshops, warehouses and commercial businesses form part of the area's economic landscape.

🏢 MUNICIPAL FLATS

Woodhurst's blocks of flats form an important part of Chatsworth's housing history. We explore these distinctive residential buildings and their place within the development of Unit 10.

🏫 SCHOOLS OF WOODHURST

• Alencon Primary School
• Parkview Primary School
• Woodhurst Secondary School

We also uncover an interesting educational initiative introduced at Woodhurst Secondary School.

📚 WOODHURST LIBRARY

An important public facility serving learners, students and the surrounding community.

🏘️ WOODHURST'S RESIDENTIAL AREAS

From Woodhurst Drive and Sunset Avenue to the smaller residential streets, we capture the neighbourhood from an entirely different perspective.

────────────────────

📖 THE HISTORY OF WOODHURST

Did you know that the name Woodhurst is commonly interpreted as meaning "a wooded hill"?

The name reflects the character of the landscape on which this residential neighbourhood was developed.

Originally established as part of Chatsworth's numbered residential units, Woodhurst has grown into a community with its own distinctive institutions, businesses and landmarks.

In this episode, we explore the places that have helped shape the identity of Unit 10 and their importance to the wider Chatsworth community.

────────────────────

👇 Leave a comment and tell us what you remember about Woodhurst!

────────────────────

🚁 ABOUT CHATSWORTH FROM ABOVE

Chatsworth From Above is a documentary series by Juelz Visuelz, exploring the numbered units and surrounding communities of Chatsworth, Durban.

Through original drone cinematography, historical research and local storytelling, each episode highlights the neighbourhoods, schools, landmarks, businesses and history that have shaped Chatsworth over the decades.

entries.title: Thompsons Bay, Ballito | Charlie’s Pool & the Hole in the Wall
entries.description:
Discover Thompsons Bay, one of the best-known coastal landmarks on KwaZulu-Natal’s Dolphin Coast. Just north of Ballito, this beautiful stretch of coastline brings together sandy beaches, rugged rock formations, the Indian Ocean and the famous tidal pool known as Charlie’s Pool.

Built in 1962 by Charles de Charmoy, his family and farm labourers, the pool took around seven weeks and approximately 2,000 pockets of cement to complete. It measures about 106 metres long and 30 metres wide. More than six decades later, it remains a popular place for swimming, relaxing and snorkelling among the fish and marine life.

The Hole in the Wall is a natural rock arch beside the pool. Beyond it is a smaller beach and rocky pools where shells and marine life can be found. Access can be affected by the tide, so check local conditions before exploring the passage. 

Overlooking the bay are the white, Greek-inspired buildings of Santorini Estate, in Shaka’s Rock. The estate has access to Thompsons Bay and the neighbouring semi-private Perissa beach.

📍 Thompsons Bay, Ballito, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa

Have you visited Thompsons Bay?
Tell us what you enjoyed most: Charlie’s Pool, the beach or the Hole in the Wall.

entries.title: I caught this on a Lure  !
entries.description:
What an incredible fishing experience! In this video, I'm fishing at Warner Beach in Amanzimtoti (Toti), KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, where I manage to hook and catch a Garrick using a spoon lure!
There's nothing quite like casting an artificial lure into the ocean and feeling that exciting strike. Garrick are known for their aggressive attacks and powerful runs, making them an exciting target for saltwater lure anglers.
Join me on this fishing adventure as I share the experience of landing this beautiful fish on an artificial spoon. If you enjoy saltwater fishing, lure fishing, beach fishing, predator fishing, and outdoor adventures, this one's for you!
📍 Location: Warner Beach, Amanzimtoti (Toti), KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa

entries.title: UNIT 9: MOORTON & RISECLIFF | Chatsworth From Above
entries.description:
CHATSWORTH FROM ABOVE | EPISODE 9 — MOORTON & RISECLIFF

Our journey through Chatsworth continues, and this time we're exploring UNIT 9 — MOORTON & RISECLIFF!

After visiting Silverglen, our unofficial Unit 8, we're returning to Chatsworth's numbered residential units to discover the history, landmarks and communities that make this part of Durban unique.

But there's something interesting about Unit 9.

Although Moorton and Risecliff are closely connected, they're actually recognised as separate residential localities. And some roads commonly associated with Montford, including sections of Road 701, are also identified as Risecliff addresses.

So where does Risecliff fit into the wider Chatsworth landscape?

Join me as we take to the skies and explore the history, schools, important landmarks and changing residential landscape of Moorton and Risecliff.

📍 PLACES AND LANDMARKS FEATURED

🏫 Dawnridge Primary School
🏫 Elora Primary School
🏫 Asoka Secondary School
🏫 Risecliff Secondary School

👮 SAPS Academy Chatsworth — the South African Police Service training institution on Moorton Drive.

🛒 Moorton Shopping Centre — a familiar shopping destination serving the surrounding communities.

📚 Moorton Library — an important educational and public resource.

🏛️ Moorton Community Hall — a venue for local gatherings and activities.

⚽ Local sporting grounds and recreational areas.

🏘️ The residential neighbourhoods around Moorton Drive, Skyridge Circle, Moorcross Drive and neighbouring Risecliff.

We also explore the development of Moorton during the apartheid era, the origins of its name and an interesting historical reference that identifies Risecliff as Unit 8 — even though other accounts describe Unit 8 as missing from Chatsworth's numbered sequence.

It's another intriguing part of Chatsworth's history, and one that deserves further investigation.

────────────────────

💬 SHARE YOUR MOORTON & RISECLIFF MEMORIES!

Did you grow up in Moorton or Risecliff?

Which road did you live in? Which school did you attend?

Do you remember the old shops at Moorton Shopping Centre, the local sporting grounds or other landmarks that have changed over the years?

And how did your family distinguish between Moorton, Risecliff and Montford?

Share your memories in the comments. Your stories help preserve the history of these communities for future generations.

────────────────────

🚁 ABOUT CHATSWORTH FROM ABOVE

Chatsworth From Above is an ongoing documentary series by Juelz Visuelz, exploring the residential units and surrounding communities of Chatsworth, Durban, through aerial cinematography, historical research and local storytelling.

Each episode captures a different neighbourhood, highlighting its history, schools, landmarks, businesses, recreational spaces and community life.

From the familiar streets of home to the wider landscape of Durban, this series is a visual record of Chatsworth's past and present.

entries.title: Silverglen - The Missing Unit 8? | Chatsworth From Above
entries.description:
Welcome to another episode of Chatsworth From Above! 🚁

We've travelled from Unit 1 all the way through to Unit 7...

But what happened to Unit 8? 👀

Chatsworth's numbered sequence famously skips Unit 8, and while Silverglen was never officially designated as Unit 8, for the purpose of our journey through Chatsworth, we're having a little fun and giving Silverglen that missing spot.

Welcome to SILVERGLEN — our unofficial Unit 8!

This episode takes us high above one of the most fascinating parts of the greater Chatsworth landscape.

Unlike the numbered units we've explored previously, Silverglen has a history and character of its own, with development in the area predating the formal establishment of Chatsworth's numbered housing scheme.

From its hills, valleys and residential areas to some remarkable landmarks, we explore the Silverglen of yesterday and the community we see from above today.

Among the places featured in this episode:

📍 Silverglen Nature Reserve    
📍 The former Odeon Cinema  
📍 SCDIFA Hall  
📍 The former Sol Namara Hotel  
📍 Silverglen's residential areas and surrounding landscape

We uncover the history behind some of these landmarks, including the Odeon Cinema, which opened in 1969; the story of SCDIFA and its roots stretching back to 1914; the Sol Namara Hotel; and the remarkable natural environment preserved within Silverglen Nature Reserve.

If you grew up in Silverglen or remember the area from years gone by, add your memories to the comments. Your stories help preserve pieces of local history that aren't always found in official records.

entries.title: How Harbour Pilots Leave Massive Ships at Sea | Durban Harbour
entries.description:
Have you ever wondered how a harbour pilot gets off a massive ship after guiding it out of port?

In this video, I captured a fascinating operation at the Port of Durban — a helicopter hovering above a departing vessel before lifting the harbour pilot from the ship.

Harbour pilots play a vital role in helping large vessels safely navigate into and out of busy ports. Their specialised local knowledge allows them to work alongside the ship's captain and bridge crew as vessels navigate the harbour and its approaches.

But the action doesn't stop there.

After witnessing the helicopter pilot transfer, we'll take a look at some of the incredible vessels I've captured entering and leaving Durban Harbour — from massive cargo vessels and car carriers to impressive cruise ships.

Durban Harbour is constantly moving, and sometimes the most interesting operations are happening right in front of us without most people knowing what they're watching.

If you enjoy seeing Durban, our coastline and places around South Africa from a different perspective, subscribe to Juelz T for more.
